source_text: Quis ergo sic sceleratus et perfidus, quis sic discordiae furore uesanus, ut aut credat scindi posse aut audeat scindere unitatem Dei, uestem Domini, ecclesiam Christi? monet ipse in euangelio suo et docet dicens: et erunt unus grex et unus pastor. et esse posse uno in loco aliquis existimat aut multos pastores aut greges plures? apostolus item Paulus hanc eandem nobis insinuans unitatem obsecrat et hortatur et dicit: obsecro, inquit, uos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Iesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes et non sint in uobis schismata: sitis autem compositi in eodem sensu et in eadem sententia. et iterum dicit: sustinentes inuicem in dilectione, satis agentes seruare unitatem spiritus in coniunctione pacis. stare tu et uiuere putas posse de ecclesia recedentem, sedes sibi alias et diuersa domicilia condentem? cum dictum sit ad Rhaab, in qua praeformabatur ecclesia: patrem tuum et matrem tuam et fratres tuos et totam domum patris tui colliges ad te ipsam in domum tuam, et erit omnis qui exierit ostium domus tuae foras, reus sibi erit, item sacramentum Paschae nihil aliud in Exodi lege contineat quam ut agnus qui in figura Christi occiditur in domo una edatur. loquitur Deus dicens: in domo una comedetur, non eicietis de domo carnem foras. caro Christi et sanctum Domini eici foras non potest nec alia ulla credentibus praeter unam ecclesiam domus est. hanc domum, hoc unanimitatis hospitium designat et denuntiat Spiritus sanctus in psalmis dicens: Deus qui inhabitare facit unanimes in domo. in domo Dei, in ecclesia Christi unanimes habitant, concordes et simplices perseuerant.
thought_title: No one may tear the Church's unity
orientation: Cyprian is addressing the faithful, arguing from Scripture that the Church is one and that no one can leave it and still live.
pass_a_gloss: Who therefore so wicked and faithless, who so by [the] madness of discord insane, that either he should believe [it] can be torn or should dare to tear [the] unity of God, [the] garment of [the] Lord, [the] church of Christ? He himself warns in his gospel and teaches saying: and they will be one flock and one shepherd. And [that it] can be [that] in one place anyone thinks either many shepherds or flocks many? [The] apostle likewise Paul this same to us instilling unity beseeches and exhorts and says: I beseech, he says, you, brothers, through [the] name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that [the] same thing you say all and not be in you schisms: but be composed in [the] same mind and in [the] same judgment. And again he says: supporting [one another] in love, working [hard] to keep [the] unity of [the] spirit in [the] bond of peace. [Do] you think [that he] can stand and live departing from [the] church, seats for himself other and different dwellings founding? Since [it] was said to Rahab, in whom was prefigured [the] church: your father and your mother and your brothers and [the] whole house of your father you shall gather to yourself into your house, and it will be [that] everyone who goes out [of the] door of your house outside, guilty to himself will be, likewise [the] sacrament of [the] Passover nothing other in [the] law of Exodus contains than that [the] lamb which in [the] figure of Christ is killed in one house should be eaten. God speaks saying: in one house it shall be eaten, you shall not throw out of [the] house [the] flesh outside. [The] flesh of Christ and [the] holy [thing] of [the] Lord [to be] thrown outside not can, nor any other for believers besides [the] one church house is. This house, this lodging of unanimity designates and declares [the] Holy Spirit in [the] psalms saying: God who makes [the] unanimous to dwell in [a] house. In [the] house of God, in [the] church of Christ [the] unanimous dwell, [the] harmonious and simple persevere.

choices.why: Keeps the clothing metaphor from the previous section's tunic imagery; 'garment' is literal for uestem and avoids the glossary term 'tunic' which is reserved for tunica.
Literal rendering of the quoted Gospel words; preserves the singular emphasis on unity.
rejected: a single flock and a single shepherd

choices.english: you all say the same thing
choices.why: Literal rendering of the Pauline phrase; 'the same thing' captures id ipsum exactly.
Standard literal rendering of coniunctio as 'bond'; preserves the Pauline phrase.
Literal rendering of the legal phrase; 'for himself' preserves the dative of disadvantage.
Hospitium as 'lodging' keeps the house/dwelling imagery; 'unanimity' is the literal sense of unanimitas.

pass_b_english: Who, then, is so wicked and faithless, who is so mad with the fury of discord, that he could believe the unity of God can be split, or dare to split it—the garment of the Lord, the Church of Christ? The Lord himself warns and teaches in his Gospel, saying: "And there will be one flock and one shepherd" (John 10:16). Does anyone think that in one place there can be either many shepherds or many flocks? The apostle Paul likewise, insinuating this same unity to us, entreats and urges, saying: "I entreat you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing and that there be no schisms among you; but be composed in the same mind and in the same judgment" (1 Corinthians 1:10). And again he says: "Sustaining one another in love, making every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Ephesians 4:2-3). Do you think you can stand and live while departing from the Church, building other seats and different dwellings for yourself? For it was said to Rahab, in whom the Church was prefigured: "You will gather your father and your mother and your brothers and the whole house of your father to yourself in your house, and everyone who goes out the door of your house outside will be guilty for himself" (Joshua 2:18-19). Likewise, the sacred sign of the Passover in the law of Exodus contains nothing other than that the lamb, which is killed as a figure of Christ, is eaten in one house. God speaks, saying: "It will be eaten in one house; you will not throw the flesh outside the house" (Exodus 12:46). The flesh of Christ and the holy thing of the Lord cannot be thrown outside, and there is no other house for believers except the one Church. This house, this lodging of unanimity, the Holy Spirit designates and declares in the Psalms, saying: "God, who makes the unanimous dwell in a house" (Psalm 68:6). In the house of God, in the Church of Christ, the unanimous dwell, and the harmonious and simple persevere.

last_rejected.source_quote: Deus qui inhabitare facit unanimes in domo
last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 67:7 or 68:7, not 68:6. The Hebrew/English numbering for this psalm: LXX Psalm 67 is English Psalm 68. The verse 'God sets the solitary in families' (KJV) or 'God makes a home for the lonely' is Psalm 68:6 in Hebrew numbering, but the Latin 'Deus qui inhabitare facit unanimes in domo' corresponds to LXX 67:7. In Hebrew numbering this is Psalm 68:6. So the citation is actually correct in Hebrew numbering.
last_rejected.fix: Psalm 68:6 is correct in Hebrew numbering
last_rejected.ruling: Claim itself admits citation is correct in Hebrew/English numbering (Psalm 68:6); not a real error.
